Build the training folders for BirdNET-Analyzer

Source: R/training.R
build_training_set.Rd

Splits the reviewed clips into a training and a test set and copies them into the folder layout that the training script of BirdNET-Analyzer expects: one folder per class, named after the label (species_code, so the retrained classifier keeps the labels of the current one), with the negatives of a class in a folder with the same name prefixed by - (or all negatives in one non-event folder; see Negatives). The test clips go to a separate test folder; with val_prop, a validation set by night goes to val, to be passed as --test_data (see Splits).

Usage

build_training_set(
  validation,
  output_dir,
  split = c("site", "night", "site_species_night", "none"),
  test_sites = NULL,
  test_prop = 0.2,
  seed = 2026,
  max_per_site_species = NULL,
  exclude_from_test = NULL,
  val_prop = NULL,
  val_seed = seed + 1,
  negatives = TRUE,
  negatives_folder = NULL,
  min_files = 100,
  copy = TRUE,
  remap_from = NULL,
  remap_to = NULL,
  strict = FALSE
)

Arguments

validation

Reviewed clips, as returned by classify_review(), post_validation() ($validation) or read_validation_tables(). It needs site, species_code, clip_file, verdict and reviewed_path (the path where the review left each clip), and night for the splits by night.

output_dir

Output folder; train/ and, if any clip is held out, test/ are created in it.

split

How to split the clips into training and test sets; see Splits.

test_sites

Sites held out for testing with split = "site". NULL puts every clip in train/.

test_prop

Proportion of the nights of each site (or site x species) drawn for the test set.

seed

Seed of the draws.

max_per_site_species

Optional maximum number of positive training clips per site x species. Larger sets are reduced by taking clips from the nights in turn, in random order, which keeps as many nights as possible. Test clips and negatives are not reduced.

exclude_from_test

Optional table with site and night (e.g. from training_nights()): nights that must not be in the test set, such as nights whose recordings trained another classifier that will be compared on it. They are left out of the draws of the test and validation sets and stay in the training set.

val_prop

Optional proportion of the training nights of each site drawn for the validation set (val/); see Splits. NULL draws none.

val_seed

Seed of the validation draw. The default, seed + 1, is also the seed of max_per_site_species; the two draws are separate, and the default reproduces the training sets of the FrogNet project.

negatives

Include the negative clips?

negatives_folder

NULL puts the negatives of each class in a -<species_code> folder. A non-event class of BirdNET-Analyzer ("Noise", "Other", "Background" or "Silence") puts all of them in that folder instead; see Negatives.

min_files

Minimum number of positive training files per class below which a warning is raised.

copy

Copy the clips? With FALSE, only training_set.csv is written, so that the split can be built on a computer without the clips and copied later.

remap_from, remap_to

Optional prefix of reviewed_path and its replacement, for clips reviewed on another computer or drive.

strict

Raise an error if any check is above 0?

Value

A tibble with one row per clip: site, species_code, verdict, set ("train", "val" or "test"), class_folder, clip_file, source_audio, clip_start, clip_end, from, to and night, invisibly, with the checks in the attribute "checks". With copy = TRUE, clips that could not be copied are left out.

Details

The layout follows the documentation of BirdNET-Analyzer (version 2.4.0, birdnet_analyzer.train), which also recommends at least 100 files per species; classes below min_files in the training set raise a warning. Whole-recording clips of "random_recordings" (longer than 3 s, confidence = NA) are left out: their label says only that the species was heard somewhere in the recording.

The table of clips is also written to training_set.csv in output_dir; keep it with the classifier, to leave these clips out of later validation rounds with exclude_training_clips().

Splits

Clips of the same night are correlated, so a split by clip leaks information from the training into the test set.

  • "site": the clips of test_sites form the test set, which then measures transfer to sites the classifier was not trained on.

  • "night": in each site, ceiling(n * test_prop) of its n nights are drawn for the test set, for all species together, so that no recording is training data for one species and test data for another.

  • "site_species_night": the nights are drawn within each site x species with at least two nights (the split of the 2.x scripts of the FrogNet project). The same night can then be in the training set for one species and in the test set for another, which breaks the independence of the test set; it is kept only to reproduce earlier training sets, and warns.

  • "none": every clip goes to the training set.

With val_prop, a validation set is drawn after the test set and after max_per_site_species, among the nights left in the training set: in each site, ceiling(n * val_prop) of its n training nights, never from exclude_from_test. Its clips go to val/. BirdNET-Analyzer draws its own validation set by file, which leaks nights, and its autotune chooses the hyperparameters on it; pass val/ as --test_data so that the validation is by night, and keep test/ for the final evaluation. The result is the same as a second call of build_training_set() with split = "night", test_prop = val_prop and seed = val_seed on the training rows of the first.

The draws use seed (seed + 1 for max_per_site_species, and val_seed for the validation set) and leave the global random number generator as it was. They follow the order of the rows of validation: the same clips in another order give another split.

Negatives

BirdNET-Analyzer (version 2.4.0 and its main branch of October 2026) gives the label -1 to the clips of -<species_code> folders. That label enters the loss functions unchanged, which makes the loss of those clips negative and unbounded; keras.metrics.AUC does not count -1 as a negative, which inflates the validation AUPRC whenever the validation set holds such clips; and the internal random split puts all of them in the training set. Clips of the non-event folders ("Noise", "Other", "Background", "Silence", in any case) get the label 0 and do not have these problems (reported in https://github.com/birdnet-team/BirdNET-Analyzer/issues/1033). Until it is fixed, use negatives_folder = "Noise": every negative goes to that folder, as <species>-<site>-<clip_file> (the short species code after the last _ of species_code), so that the file keeps its origin and clips of different species do not collide. The negatives then train the classifier against all classes, not only their own.

Checks

At the end, the counts are reported, and kept in the attribute "checks" of the result: test nights (site x night) that also have training clips, test nights listed in exclude_from_test, and test clips that overlap a training clip of the same species in the same recording; with val_prop, also validation nights with training clips and validation nights listed in exclude_from_test. All should be 0 with split = "night". With strict = TRUE, any count above 0 is an error.

See also

training_nights(), exclude_training_clips(), vignette("retraining").
